newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rican cancer victims in radiation accident.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rican cancer victims in radiation accident.

text.p: The lives of 109 cancer victims in Costa Rica were in danger after an accidental radiation overdose during treatment, a senior medical official said on Saturday.
"Ths is a national tragedy," Alvaro Salas, head of the state Social Security Institute, told Reuters.

He said the accident was detected after the victims, including seven children, who had undergone radiation treatment in the hospital of San Juan de Dios in San Jose, suffered unusual diarrhoea, skin infections and inflamation of the mucous membrane in the mouth and stomach.
Salas said there was an error in calibrating one of the pumps of radioactive cobalt used in the treatment, which meant the patients were over-exposed to radioactive material.
They had been urgently called back for tests by international specialists, he said, adding that the full impact of the error would not be known until next week.

Those affected had undergone treatment between Sept. 26 and 27, Salas said. Cobalt has been used in radiation treatment to destroy cancer cells in Costa Rica since 1969, used in conjunction with chemotherapy, he added.
